builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
summary: DexPort replaces full robot-arm teleoperation and human-motion retargeting with a portable interface built from the same dexterous hand used at deployment, recording commanded joint targets and measured states while the operator controls wrist motion and selects finger skills. The cost is specialized high-DoF robot-hand hardware, a skill set that must be designed per hand, and behavior-cloning training that requires thousands of demonstrations (over 2,500 collected here), plus a camera and compute for visuomotor policy training. Failure modes include operator skill-selection errors propagating into demonstrations, limited skill coverage for tasks outside the designed repertoire, and policies that inherit the hand's embodiment specificity so they do not transfer to other robot hands.
rationale: This is a robotics hardware and data-collection system requiring a physical dexterous hand and real-world deployment, which falls outside the production scope of an AI/ML engineer working with a single GPU or third-party APIs.
technique: Portable hand-held skill interface for dexterous demonstration collection

claims.statement: DexPort replaces full robot-arm teleoperation and human-motion retargeting with a portable interface built from the same dexterous hand used at deployment, recording commanded joint targets and measured states while the operator controls wrist motion and selects finger skills. The cost is specialized high-DoF robot-hand hardware, a skill set that must be designed per hand, and behavior-cloning training that requires thousands of demonstrations (over 2,500 collected here), plus a camera and compute for visuomotor policy training. Failure modes include operator skill-selection errors propagating into demonstrations, limited skill coverage for tasks outside the designed repertoire, and policies that inherit the hand's embodiment specificity so they do not transfer to other robot hands.

Behavior cloning success improves from 11% to 64% when training on recorded robot commands instead of joint states, and from 36% to 78% when including in-the-wild data; these are point improvements in task success rate, not multiplicative factors.
